discovery: Programmable quantum matter with individually controlled Rydberg atoms in optical tweezer arrays

nominees.name: Antoine Browaeys
nominees.affiliation: Laboratoire Charles Fabry, Institut d'Optique / CNRS, Palaiseau, France

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / quantum simulation and quantum information
motivation: The nominees turned the Rydberg dipole blockade from a theoretical idea into a controlled tool for engineering interactions between single neutral atoms. Saffman and Browaeys reported the first observations of blockade between two individually trapped atoms (2009) and used it to entangle them and build neutral-atom quantum gates. Browaeys and Lukin then built defect-free, reconfigurable arrays of hundreds of tweezer-trapped atoms. With them they realized programmable quantum simulators of Ising and XY magnetism, observed quantum many-body scars, prepared topological spin liquids, and ran error-detected logical-qubit circuits. Every atom is placed, addressed and read out one by one. This brings the single-quantum control of cavity QED to strongly interacting many-body systems. It has opened a new experimental route to quantum phase transitions, non-equilibrium dynamics and scalable quantum computing, and it is a direct heir of the European atomic-physics tradition.
